We teach the children how to use their creativity and imagination to design, make and evaluate products that solve a problem or fit a design brief. In doing this, we equip the children with problem-solving skills, and increase resilience whilst drawing on a broad range of subject knowledge.: Take inspiration from designs through history.

Welcome to our website!
Welcome
Head of School – Mrs S Hamer
On behalf of all the children, the staff and governors, I would like to welcome you to South Lake Primary School’s website.
Our website brings together everything you need to know about our school — from practical details like our staff team and school uniform to what the children learn and how we keep them safe.
Admissions
We admit 60 children each year to Reception and this is our Planned Admission number (PAN) for each year group. We still have places for Reception children, due to the low birth rates in the area.

Early Years - Nursery and Reception​
Rated Outstanding, our EYFS provision offers the foundations for a lifetime of learning, curiosity and confidence. We offer a safe, nurturing and inspiring environment where every child is valued and celebrated.
At South Lake, we foster independence, resilience, and creativity, ensuring every child develops a love for learning from their very first steps into education.
'The school has meticulously planned a wealth of opportunities that enable pupils to celebrate their various strengths.' Ofsted 2025
We place a significant emphasis on language and oracy. We promote this through giving prompts for questions, targeted questioning, echo talk and group discussions. Integrating oracy as a central element in developing the steps to success, aligned with the four strands of oracy (cognitive, linguistic, physical and emotional) is paramount to children's learning.
The principles that guide the work in the EYFS are grouped into 4 themes:
The EYFS Curriculum consists of the seven areas of Learning and Development; three core and four specific areas.
The three prime areas of learning are:
Inspiring learning through play
At South Lake Reception, every child is part of one nurturing community. With the freedom to explore both classrooms and outdoor spaces, children enjoy a creative curriculum that celebrates individuality, encourages curiosity, and inspires sustained learning through play.”
"We provide a thoughtfully planned continuous provision that offers children a consistent, safe, and stimulating environment in which to explore and extend their learning. This approach encourages independence, supports confident decision-making, and promotes curiosity.
Welcome to South Lake Nursery 🌟
At South Lake, we believe every child is unique, curious, and full of potential. Our nursery provides a warm, nurturing environment where children feel safe, valued, and inspired to learn.
Through our carefully designed creative curriculum, children enjoy the freedom to explore, discover, and develop at their own pace. From engaging indoor activities to rich outdoor learning experiences, we encourage imagination, independence, and a lifelong love of learning.
Our supportive adults nurture each child’s confidence, communication, and creativity while celebrating their individual interests. Through play-based learning, children build strong academic foundations and develop the social and emotional skills essential for future success.
In the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS), we teach reading through a systematic synthetic phonics approach, following the Little Wandle Letters and Sounds programme. This approach is consistently embedded across the school to strengthen and consolidate pupils’ learning. During daily phonics sessions, children revisit prior knowledge while also developing and applying new skills through carefully structured, engaging activities.
Reading is nurtured through regular shared book experiences, where adults model fluency, expression, and the exploration of new vocabulary. Children have access to a rich and diverse collection of carefully chosen core texts to inspire a love of reading and broaden their experiences. In addition, adults work with small groups of pupils, providing focused support to ensure steady progress in reading skills.
At South Lake, we follow the Mastering Number and White Rose Maths programmes, designed to help every child understand, enjoy, and succeed in mathematics. Our approach focusses on building deep understanding, taking learning one step at a time to ensure strong foundations. Through practical activities, children develop confidence and a genuine enjoyment of maths that supports their long-term success.
At South Lake, our Forest School offers every child the chance to explore and learn through engaging, hands-on experiences in the natural environment. These sessions help children build confidence, self-esteem, and a sense of responsibility for both their surroundings and one another. We encourage them to make thoughtful, independent choices and to take appropriate, calculated risks, helping them develop awareness, resilience, and care for their own and others’ safety.

Early Years - Nursery and Reception​

French
At South Lake Primary we believe that the learning of a modern foreign language provides a valuable educational, social and culture experience for our pupils. The intention of our French curriculum is to foster an interest in other cultures and languages, the ultimate aim being that pupils will feel willing and able to continue studying languages beyond key stage 2
We use the Language Angels scheme of work and resources to support us in our offering of a relevant, broad and vibrant foreign languages curriculum that will inspire and excite our pupils using a wide variety of topics and themes. We will embed the essential skills of listening, reading, speaking and writing which will draw on the foundations of our pupils’ oracy learning and extend their understanding of how language works.
Whilst it is not statutory to learn a modern foreign language before year 3, we strongly believe that the best language learning begins at an early age. Learning new sounds, listening to stories and appreciating songs in French will help our pupils gain confidence and give them the best possible chance at developing fluency from Year 3 upwards. We begin by learning simple greetings and build on this each year. We identify where France is in the world and learn that French is spoken in many countries.
In addition, we have a progression document, which shows the skills and knowledge your child will be taught in each unit of work. Please click on the links below to see these.
Les Non Négociables (Our non-negotiables)
In addition to covering a variety of topics through the Language Angels scheme, we also believe in the importance of life skills. As French is our chosen language we have identified a set of non-negotiables (Les Non Négociables) which we believe every child should be confident in when they leave us for their secondary school journey. Not only will these prepare them for KS3 learning but they will also prepare them for visiting a French speaking country.
Bonjour, je m’appelle ...
Hello, my name is ...
Ask how someone is and respond with how they are.
Où sont les toilettes?

Art
We believe that Art promotes physical and psychological well-being. It enables children to express themselves and to appreciate works made by others. Art nurtures creativity and it engages children in a process that develops self-esteem, self-discipline, cooperation, and self-motivation. To do this, children need to be taught specific Art skills, in a sequential way, giving them the confidence and the tools to explore their own ideas.
To build an art curriculum where children can develop both their subject knowledge and progression of skills, our art lessons are underpinned by three main areas. In these the pupils are taught to:
• Develop ideas – understanding how ideas develop through an artistic process
• Master techniques – developing procedural knowledge so that ideas may be communicated
• Take inspiration from the greats – learning from both the artistic process and techniques of great artists and artisans throughout history.

Design technology
At South Lake Primary School, we aim to ensure that our children gain the knowledge to think, speak and act like a designer, a constructor and evaluator. We teach the children how to use their creativity and imagination to design, make and evaluate products that solve a problem or fit a design brief. In doing this, we equip the children with problem-solving skills, and increase resilience whilst drawing on a broad range of subject knowledge.
The key Design Technology skills and concepts are:
In Year 1 the focus is on completing a variety of creative and practical activities while drawing on design skills. In Year 1 the children make sliding pictures, using cardboard and fabric to make puppets. In doing this the children use a variety of materials, such as different textiles and make use of different tools and equipment. The children learn practical skills, such as cutting, shaping, joining and finishing to make levers and slides. There is an emphasis on teaching the children to ask themselves, how could I improve their product? In Cooking and Nutrition, the children learn to cut, peel and grate various fruits and vegetables.
In Year 2 the focus moves onto acquiring more technical knowledge, as the children learn to build structures, such as a bridge and vehicle. They also explore the use of mechanisms, by making their own axis and chassis, by drawing and then evaluating their product. They learn how to make changes to their design and make it a more stable structure. In Cooking and Nutrition, they learn the basic principles of healthy eating and understanding where food comes from, by growing their own vegetables and fruit.
In Year 3 the focus is on creating things that are inspired by more in depth research. The children must design products based on research that they complete and come up with cross-sectional drawings, as well as annotate their designs. They expand on their key stage 1 knowledge and skills and make an aqueduct, a puppet show as well as a pencil case. In doing this they rely on different materials and select from a range of tools and equipment to complete the task. In Cooking and Nutrition, they design a healthy and balanced pasta based meal, drawing on their Science knowledge of food groups.
In Year 4 the primary focus is teaching the children to understand and how to use mechanical and electrical systems in their products. The children design a product for their use that includes a lever and linkage system. They also design a torch, and ultimately rely on computer aided designs to complete the making of the product. In Cooking and nutrition, the children design a vegetarian savoury meal centred around seasonality.
In Year 5 the children continue to build on their knowledge of mechanical systems. They make cam toys and a Victorian puppet show. Both draw on a variety of tools and equipment, as well as a great selection of materials. In Cooking and Nutrition, the children design a menu, drawing on the food that the Mayans ate. This involves a great deal of research, and it draws on the History that they have learnt about the Mayan culture.
n Year 6 the focus is on an interdisciplinary approach to Design and Technology as the skills acquired become integrated across all designs. The children complete tasks in a broad variety of contexts; from designing Greek sandals, to Gingerbread houses, as well as making their own biomes and a wartime teddy. The making of all these items involves a great deal of research and the children develop their ideas through discussion and sketches. In Cooking and Nutrition they make carrot ration buns, building on their history topic of World War II.

Forest School
At South Lake Primary school our Forest School provides a nurturing space that supports our children’s wellbeing by providing positive, outdoor child centred experiences in a natural setting.
The Forest School philosophy promotes holistic, long-term, child-centered learning in an outdoor, natural environment. It fosters self-esteem, confidence, and independence through supported risk-taking, hands-on experiences, and the development of strong relationships with nature and peers. Unlike one-off outdoor trips, it emphasizes ongoing sessions where children direct their own learning and exploration, encouraging a lifelong love of nature.
Children are active, take ownership of their learning and develop their self-esteem through a variety of activities. The children work together to problem solve in many different ways, taking into account one another’s ideas and learn to work together to achieve a positive outcome. The children have the opportunity to experience nature in a hands on, safe, secure and supported environment but also have the chance to manage their own risks and set their own challenges.
We have our own wooded area on the school grounds where we have Forest School sessions; exploring, building, climbing, story telling, making art and creating fire!

Sports Premium
We love sports at South Lake! We believe that all children should be given opportunities to take part in different sports, as the impact on their mental well-being as well as their physical fitness can be life-long. South Lake is lucky to have qualified sports leaders who take curriculum lessons and after-school clubs and teams.
For children who show a particular aptitude, we compete in local and district leagues , with teams representing us in sports such as football, table tennis, tag rugby and kurling.
In year 5, the children have swimming lessons with qualified staff at a local pool. This is part of the curriculum offer and a contribution towards travel costs is the only request from parents/carers. In year 6, 90% of our children are able to swim 25 metres unaided, using a recognisable stroke.
The PE and Sports Premium is designed to help primary schools improve the quality of sports provision they offer pupils so that all pupils can develop healthy lifestyles.
